title: fix(rest,runtime)!: the import doors and the catalog refresh read the walled-catalog verdict the metadata save door reads
body:
Clause-②: no (narrowing) — under the `isolated` and `group` tenancy postures, importing a remote table as an object (`POST /api/v1/datasources/:name/external/tables/:remote/import`, and the MCP `import_object` tool) and refreshing a federated datasource's cached catalog (`POST /api/v1/datasources/:name/external/refresh-catalog`) are writes to the environment's metadata catalog, and they are the platform operator's, as every other write to that catalog is.
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: none — no `skills/**` text teaches any of the three doors or who may call them (0 hits for the import route, the refresh route, `refreshCatalog` and `import_object` under `skills/`; `datasource` itself is named there, the positive control); the rule is stated in the docs this diff updates (`content/docs/deployment/tenancy-modes.mdx`, `content/docs/data-modeling/odata-datasources.mdx`).

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：三道写入门——REST 远程表导入路由、MCP `import_object` 工具、REST 外部目录刷新路由——在 `isolated` / `group` 租户姿态下，与元数据保存门问同一个“围墙目录写入”裁决。
- 为什么改：导入把一个对象存进环境共享的元数据目录，目录刷新把数据源的 `external_catalog` 快照存进同一个目录；围墙姿态下这个目录只归平台运营方（与引擎自身）写，所以这三道门与保存门读同一条裁决。
- 风险与回滚：围墙姿态下，平台运营方以下的调用方导入或刷新目录改为 `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`，什么都不读取、不保存；租户服务已注册却答不出时回 `503`；`single` 与未注册租户服务的部署不变；回滚即还原本 PR，已导入的对象与已存的快照不受影响。
- 先看：`packages/rest/src/external-datasource-routes.ts`（`refuseFederationRequest` 的 `catalogWrite` 段，导入与刷新两条路由共用）、`packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts`（`federationService` 的 `catalogWrite` 段）、`packages/qa/dogfood/test/external-import-walled-catalog-refusal.dogfood.test.ts`。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/dogfood exec vitest run test/external-import-walled-catalog-refusal.dogfood.test.ts`，预期 9 个用例全部通过（围墙下三道门拒绝、运营方可导入与刷新、`single` 下照常导入与刷新）。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。

## What changes

- **The rule.** Under `isolated` and `group` every organization shares the environment's metadata catalog, and a write to it is admitted only for the platform operator and for the engine's own writes (ADR-0131 D3, D12 items 7–8, D11). Three doors of the federation family write that catalog: the import of a remote table as an object, at the REST route and at the MCP `import_object` tool, saves an `object`; the catalog refresh at the REST route saves the datasource's `external_catalog` snapshot. Each of them now asks the walled-catalog verdict the metadata save door asks (`walledCatalogWriteVerdict`, `@objectstack/metadata-core`) for the type it writes, after the federation family's capability rule and before the federation service is looked up.
- **The answer.** A refused call answers `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` with the verdict's sentence for the type written, which is the sentence the metadata save door answers, naming the posture. Nothing is introspected and nothing is saved. A `tenancy` service that is registered and cannot answer refuses the call `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, never a permit.
- **Unchanged.** The platform operator imports and refreshes under a wall as before. Under `single`, and on a deployment with no `tenancy` service, every caller holding both federation capabilities imports and refreshes as before. Listing remote tables, drafting an object and validating are unchanged, and the federation capability rule answers first, as before.
- **Docs.** `deployment/tenancy-modes` lists the import and the catalog refresh among the walled writes; `data-modeling/odata-datasources` states who imports and refreshes under a wall; row 55b of the system-context census names the doors, with its register regenerated. The `walledCatalogWriteVerdict` doc comment and its ADR anchor name the three doors among the doors that ask it.

## Tests

- `packages/rest/src/external-datasource-routes-auth-guard.test.ts`: for the import route and for the catalog refresh route alike, under `group` and `isolated` an administrator holding both federation capabilities is refused `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` before the service is looked up; the sentence equals the verdict's sentence for the type the route writes (`object`, `external_catalog`); the capability rule still answers first; listing is still served; the platform operator and the `single` / no-tenancy controls are served; a failing `tenancy` service answers `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`.
- `packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp-federation-bridge.test.ts`: the same rule, refusals and controls at the MCP `import_object` bridge.
- `packages/rest/src/rest-write-route-hook-refusal-sentence.ledger.test.ts`: the ledger's context registers no `tenancy` service, as on a deployment that is not walled, so its import rows still reach the federation service the ledger reads.
- `packages/qa/dogfood/test/external-import-walled-catalog-refusal.dogfood.test.ts`: a booted showcase under `group` with the federation service and the MCP server mounted. An organization administrator holding both capabilities is refused at the REST import door and at the catalog refresh with the save door's status and sentence for the type written, and at `import_object` (a real OAuth agent token granted `metadata:write` and `actions:execute`) with the same code and sentence; nothing is saved or stored. Controls: the platform operator imports at both import doors and refreshes the catalog under the same wall; under `single` the same kind of administrator does each as before.

## Acceptance notes

- **Where the rule sits: at the doors, not in the shared save path.** The save path below the doors (`saveMetaItem` behind `importObject`, the catalog persistence behind `refreshCatalog`) receives the item, not the caller's rung or whether the caller is the engine, so judging there would mean threading the caller into the federation service contract. The doors are where caller admission already lives in this family (the capability rule runs there), so the walled verdict runs beside it and refuses before any landing is resolved or any remote schema is read. On the REST side the two write routes share the one guard (`refuseFederationRequest`), each naming the type it writes.
- **The code.** The status and the sentence are the save door's. The code is `PERMISSION_DENIED`, the standard-catalog member this family already answers for a 403; the REST `/meta` door answers its grandfathered synonym (`STANDARD_SYNONYM_WAIVERS`, ADR-0112 D3), which keeps a wire value and is not endorsed for new code.
- **Breaking, patch.** An accept-set narrowing under a walled posture only; no key of any schema moves and nothing stored changes, so both packages take a patch with a BREAKING banner (ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`). The changeset names all three doors.

## Verification
